Yes — there’s one big roadmap area we haven’t mapped yet: the actual conversation + composer DOM.

Our current body fixtures intentionally removed <main> content, which was correct for safety, but the roadmap later needs message bookmarks, navigator, timestamps, copying, image/code tools, draft protection, collapsing, counters, prompt tools, etc.

So I’d make one final future-proof capture batch, then stop collecting DOM until a feature actually needs something new.

1. Generic conversation-message capture

Use this same script multiple times.

Run it, then click inside the message/content you want captured.

JavaScript
(() => {
  const filename = prompt(
    "Fixture filename",
    "chatgpt-message-assistant-basic.html"
  );

  if (!filename) return;

  console.log("ARMED: click inside the message you want to capture.");

  const handler = event => {
    const target = event.target;

    const turn =
      target.closest?.('[data-message-author-role]') ??
      target.closest?.('[data-testid^="conversation-turn"]') ??
      target.closest?.('[data-message-id]') ??
      target.closest?.('article');

    if (!turn) {
      console.warn("That click was not inside a recognizable conversation turn.");
      return;
    }

    document.removeEventListener("click", handler, true);
    event.preventDefault();
    event.stopPropagation();

    const html = turn.outerHTML;

    const blob = new Blob([html], {
      type: "text/html;charset=utf-8"
    });

    const url = URL.createObjectURL(blob);
    const a = document.createElement("a");

    a.href = url;
    a.download = filename;

    document.body.appendChild(a);
    a.click();
    a.remove();

    setTimeout(() => URL.revokeObjectURL(url), 1000);

    console.log("Saved:", filename, turn);
  };

  document.addEventListener("click", handler, true);
})();

Use it to make these:

chatgpt-message-user-basic.html
chatgpt-message-assistant-basic.html
chatgpt-message-assistant-code.html
chatgpt-message-assistant-citation.html
chatgpt-message-assistant-image.html
chatgpt-message-user-attachment.html
example-source.html

Very basic instructions:

User basic

Find any normal message you sent → click its text.

Assistant basic

Find a normal text response → click its text.

Code

Find an assistant response containing a proper code block → click inside the code block.

This directly supports the roadmap's code-block features.

Citation

Find an assistant message containing ChatGPT citations/source links → click the response.

Useful because Better Copying explicitly wants to remove UI-only citation junk where appropriate.

Generated image

Find a chat containing an image generated by ChatGPT → click the image area.

That maps the future image-QoL target.

User attachment

Find one of your messages where you uploaded a file/image → click the attachment/card.

Useful for exports and media handling.

Tool output

Find an assistant turn where ChatGPT visibly used a tool or rendered a special tool/result card → click inside it.

Useful because Message Collapsing explicitly includes tool outputs.

If one of those types is annoying to find, skip it for now. We can capture it when we naturally encounter one.

2. Composer states

These are worth capturing because Draft Protection, Prompt Library insertion, counters, Enhance Prompt and AI Write Prompt all eventually interact with the composer.

Run this, then click inside the ChatGPT typing box:

JavaScript
(() => {
  const filename = prompt(
    "Fixture filename",
    "chatgpt-composer-empty.html"
  );

  if (!filename) return;

  console.log("ARMED: click inside the ChatGPT composer.");

  const handler = event => {
    const target = event.target;

    const composer =
      target.closest?.('[data-type="unified-composer"]') ??
      target.closest?.('form') ??
      target.closest?.('[contenteditable="true"]')?.parentElement?.parentElement;

    if (!composer) {
      console.warn("Could not resolve the composer from that click.");
      return;
    }

    document.removeEventListener("click", handler, true);
    event.preventDefault();
    event.stopPropagation();

    const blob = new Blob([composer.outerHTML], {
      type: "text/html;charset=utf-8"
    });

    const url = URL.createObjectURL(blob);
    const a = document.createElement("a");

    a.href = url;
    a.download = filename;

    document.body.appendChild(a);
    a.click();
    a.remove();

    setTimeout(() => URL.revokeObjectURL(url), 1000);

    console.log("Saved:", filename, composer);
  };

  document.addEventListener("click", handler, true);
})();

Make these three:

chatgpt-composer-empty.html
chatgpt-composer-with-draft.html
chatgpt-composer-with-attachment.html

For draft, type something disposable like:

Wolf Expansion fixture test draft

but do not send it.

For attachment, attach some harmless dummy file/image, leave it sitting in the composer, and capture.

3. Native Search dialog

This one isn't mandatory for implementing Better Conversation Search, because ours can be extension-owned, but it is useful for matching ChatGPT's search styling and navigation behavior. The roadmap gives search a pretty significant role.

Open ChatGPT's normal Search, leave it open, then:

JavaScript
(() => {
  const dialogs = [...document.querySelectorAll('[role="dialog"]')]
    .filter(el =>
      el.getClientRects().length > 0 &&
      !el.closest('[data-wolf-expansion]')
    );

  if (!dialogs.length) {
    console.warn("No visible native dialog found.");
    return;
  }

  const dialog = dialogs[dialogs.length - 1];

  const blob = new Blob([dialog.outerHTML], {
    type: "text/html;charset=utf-8"
  });

  const url = URL.createObjectURL(blob);
  const a = document.createElement("a");

  a.href = url;
  a.download = "chatgpt-search-dialog.html";

  document.body.appendChild(a);
  a.click();
  a.remove();

  setTimeout(() => URL.revokeObjectURL(url), 1000);

  console.log("Saved ChatGPT Search dialog:", dialog);
})();

After that, I think we're done

I wouldn't proactively capture Dashboard, Tags, Notes, Trash, Smart Folders, Local AI, backup/sync, etc. Those are largely Wolf-owned UIs/data systems; they don't require reverse-mapping ChatGPT DOM.

Likewise the native companion, cloud sync, embeddings, AI providers, publishing, licensing, storage model, performance, etc. are architectural rather than DOM-dependent.

So the remaining capture wishlist is basically:

Conversation
├─ normal user message
├─ normal assistant message
├─ code response
├─ citation response
├─ generated image response
├─ user attachment
└─ tool output

Composer
├─ empty
├─ unsent draft
└─ attachment present

Native UI
└─ Search dialog

That plus the fixtures we already made gives us coverage for essentially every roadmap area where knowing ChatGPT's DOM ahead of time is genuinely useful.

Upload the raw captures here afterward and I'll do the same sanitization + clean filenames + safety scan + one ZIP treatment before any of them touch Git. 🐺
